title: A Phone Call About a Sunrise on the Mountain
script: Rafi: [excited] Mom, I have to tell you about this morning. I woke up before dawn to watch the sunrise from the mountain.
Mother: That sounds lovely. Was it worth waking up so early?
Rafi: [amazed] Completely worth it. The sky turned pink, then orange, then this bright gold, all in about twenty minutes.
Mother: I can almost picture it. Were you alone up there, or with friends?
Rafi: [quietly] With two friends, but honestly, none of us spoke much. We just sat there watching, in silence.
Mother: What did it feel like, being up so high with a view like that?
Rafi: [softly] Small, in a good way. Like my worries from this week suddenly felt much less important.
Mother: That's exactly what nature does sometimes. It can help us see our worries in a new way.
Rafi: I kept thinking, how does something this beautiful happen every single morning, and most people never even see it.
Mother: [thoughtful] We get used to beauty when it's constant. The sun rises daily, so we forget to look up.
Rafi: I want to remember to look up more, honestly, not just on mountains but at home too.
Mother: [encouraging] You could start small. Watch the sky for one minute from your balcony each morning.
Rafi: That's a good idea. It doesn't need to be a mountain every time.
Mother: Did you take photos? I would love to see them.
Rafi: [smiling] I took a few, but honestly, my phone camera didn't capture the real colors at all.
Mother: Some things are meant to stay only in memory, not on a screen.
Rafi: That's true. I think this morning will stay with me for a long time.
Mother: [with love] I'm so glad you got to see something so beautiful, my son. Come tell me more this weekend.
Rafi: I will, Mom. I love you. Thanks for listening to my long story about clouds and colors.
